thread:
Isabel: Hey team, just got a Priority 1 from Acme Corp — they see a sudden spike of 502/504s hitting our hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. Happening for 30% of requests in the last 20m. Customer says it started right after we enabled user-metadata headers enrichment. Trace IDs: trace-8f3a, trace-9b2c. Link to logs: https://logs.internal/acme/trace-8f3a
Ben: Thanks — can you paste a sample full request/response pair and headers (sanitized)? 502 vs 504 distinction matters (upstream reset vs timeout). Any pattern in path/model/route?
Isabel: Pasted minimal repro (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-RW-Context: eyJ1c2VyIjoiQWNtZSIsInByb21wdCI6Ii4uLiJ9... (long base64)
Content-Length: 4832
```
Response: 502, body empty. Another sample showed 504 after ~28s. Paths: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Mostly large prompts + the new X-RW-Context header present.
Carlos: Noted. Early hypothesis: header growth may be pushing Envoy/NGINX buffer or upstream h2 header size limit, causing connection reset or upstream rejection. Also could be connection pool stalls if many long-lived streams.
Dana: Customer impact summary: ~15% of their requests failing, some retries, they see user-facing timeouts. They are asking for ETA and mitigation.
Ben: Can we get envoy access logs and upstream response codes? infra-bot, can you attach the last 100 ingress logs for that customer?
infra-bot: Attached logs: https://logs.internal/ingress/acme/last-100. Sample lines show: `upstream_reset: true` and `response_code: 502` and `upstream_response_time: -` for many entries. A subset show `504` with `upstream_response_time: 28.012s`.
Carlos: OK that pattern fits two separate failure modes: upstream reset (likely header/reject) and upstream timeout (service taking too long, possibly due to overflow/backpressure). Next steps: 1) repro locally with the exact X-RW-Context payload, 2) capture Envoy error logs, 3) check ingress h2 keepalive and connection pool saturation.
Ben: I spun up a small repro calling gateway with same header; I see in envoy logs: `http2: header size 123456 exceeds max_header_bytes` in the worker log just before a reset.
Isabel: So header size limit. Which component enforces that? Envoy? NGINX? Or upstream?
Carlos: Envoy has `max_request_headers_kb` (default 60KB) and nginX may also have `large_client_header_buffers`. Our gateway uses Envoy in front of backends. Looks like newly encoded X-RW-Context with base64 JSON pushed customers above the threshold. Also some longer-tailed requests cause backend CPU to spike and hit timeouts.
Ben: Reproduced locally: when header size > 60KB envoy closes stream with a 431 or reset which surfaces as 502 in our stack. For the timeouts, the backend worker was OOMing on large prompt + metadata and GC pauses caused 504s.
Isabel: Customer wants immediate mitigation — what's safe to change?
Carlos: Quick mitigation options: 1) Rollback metadata enrichment flag for hosted API (stop sending X-RW-Context) — fast config flip. 2) Increase Envoy max header bytes cluster-wide (risky, needs deploy + testing). 3) Fail-fast on server side when header too large and return 4xx (needs app change). Short-term: flip the enrichment off for Acme and other heavy customers.
Ben: I can schedule a targeted flag rollback for Acme and a small percentage of heavy accounts via feature-gate in the edge layer. That should stop new oversized headers reaching Envoy. I estimate ~10m to flip and propagate.
Dana: Please do — communicate ETA to customer. Also, we'll prepare a postmortem and customer note.
deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: feature.edge.metadata_enrich=false for account=acme, rollout=immediate. Job ID: rb-2026-176880.
Ben: Flipped the flag at 09:42 UTC. Monitoring now.
infra-bot: Within 2m after the flip, error rate for Acme dropped from 32%->4% (502/504 combined).
Isabel: Customer reported improvement within 5m, thanks. They asked about root cause and long-term fix.
Carlos: Root cause summary for postmortem: the new metadata enrichment produced base64-encoded payloads that in some cases exceeded Envoy's header limits and also increased backend memory pressure causing timeouts. Two-pronged failure: header size -> upstream connection resets -> 502; and larger per-request memory -> backend GC/OOM -> 504.
Ben: Long-term remediation items: 1) Add server-side header size validation and return 413/431 early. 2) Add size cap and compression for X-RW-Context or move to request body/metadata store. 3) Increase observability for header sizes and per-request peak memory. 4) Add a canary and automatic rollback for metadata_enrich across heavy accounts.
Dana: I'll open a customer-facing summary and propose a follow-up that includes timeline and steps we've taken.
Ben: I'll open PRs for a short-term edge validation + a canary rollout for enrichment.
Carlos: I'll propose the Envoy config change in staging to allow graceful handling and a hard cap.
Isabel: Thanks all — marking this thread resolved for support after customer ack. :thumbsup:
Ticket update to customer: "We've temporarily disabled metadata enrichment for your account which has resolved the 502/504 spike. We're working on a permanent fix and will follow up with timeline"
Carlos: I'll own the postmortem draft. Ben, can you add the exact envoy log snippets and the rollback timeline?
Ben: Will do. Snippet for PM:
```
[2026-04-15T09:40:12Z] envoy info: http2 buffer exceed: header_bytes=65240 max=61440, resetting stream id=13
[2026-04-15T09:41:03Z] upstream reset: connection reset by peer, trace=trace-8f3a
```
Carlos: Also capturing a representative heap profile from backend at the time showing spike to 2.1GB during long prompts.
Isabel: Closing loop with customer now. Any follow-ups to track?
Dana: Follow-ups: postmortem, telemetry dashboard for header sizes, small infra change to enforce header validation in edge, and product decision on whether to keep enrichment (with size limits). I'll track.
Ben: I'll open PRs for a short-term edge validation + a canary rollout for enrichment.
Carlos: I'll propose the Envoy config change in staging to allow graceful handling and a hard cap.
Isabel: Thanks all — marking this thread resolved for support after customer ack. :thumbsup:
